original_reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
notes: All morphologies are extracted from inspected 1999 species accounts plus keyed genus characters explicitly indicated as such. Additive, no photos or source data changed. BONAP distribution deferred.

flora_morphology.growth: Glabrous annual or short-lived perennial 0.4–0.9 m
flora_morphology.leaves: Mostly alternate, linear, 2–6 mm wide; coarsely toothed edges and conspicuous yellow-brown/orange glands; aromatic
flora_morphology.cypsela: 3–3.5 mm; pappus 10–12 scales, each with 1–3 awns

source_conflicts_or_qa: Genus monotypic in original flora; oil glands and pappus structure key targets.

flora_morphology.leaves: Basal and lower narrow lanceolate, usually >5 times as long as wide and 1–4+ cm wide, tapering to petiole; entire
flora_morphology.heads: Large terminal solitary heads with pointed stiff receptacular chaff
flora_morphology.rays: Light pink/purplish or white, typically 2–4 cm and spreading, not strongly reflexed; ray limbs sterile
flora_morphology.discs: Fertile, pollen yellow; disk with rigid spiny scales

source_conflicts_or_qa: Flora recognizes species despite intergradation with E. pallida; var. strigosa not separated here.
E. pallida generally drooping longer rays 4–9 cm and white pollen per flora key.

flora_morphology.growth: Low annual, prostrate to upright, freely branched, appressed-scabrous pubescence
flora_morphology.leaves: Opposite, sessile or short-petiolate, lanceolate/narrow elliptic, nearly entire to slightly toothed
flora_morphology.heads: Small short-peduncled terminal and upper-axillary heads
flora_morphology.rays: Numerous fertile rays with narrow ~1 mm white ligules
flora_morphology.fruit: Achenes 2–2.5 mm, pappus absent or inconspicuous

source_conflicts_or_qa: Source supports white tiny ray florets; do not label purely discoid.

flora_morphology.leaves: Alternate, oblanceolate-elliptic 5–18 cm long, up to 9 cm wide; basal leaves typically gone by flowering
flora_morphology.inflorescence: Glomerules of heads subtended by approximately three ovate acute leafy bracts
flora_morphology.fruit: Cylindrical achenes with forward-pointing pubescence; persistent pappus bristles dilated and hardened at base

source_conflicts_or_qa: Three leafy bracts subtend head clusters, not individual florets.

flora_morphology.growth: Densely hispid perennial from woody taproot, spreading to erect, 0.2–1 m
flora_morphology.leaves: 8–30 cm, deeply pinnately divided almost to midrib, lobes further lobed or toothed
flora_morphology.heads: Several long-peduncled radiate heads; involucre 6–10 mm high
flora_morphology.rays: Yellow ligules around 10 mm, curl under during daytime and open late afternoon through midmorning
flora_morphology.habitat: Clayey and occasionally sandy prairies; limestone outcrops

source_conflicts_or_qa: Historical name priority per original flora: peristenia published 1832; pinnatifida 1840.
Existing species card calls phyllaries multiple series; source treatment lacks this count, so not overwritten.

flora_morphology.growth: Annual per Conyza genus account, erect (30–)100–200+ cm in key
flora_morphology.leaves: Numerous alternate subsessile narrow-lanceolate/oblanceolate blades ≤14 mm wide, entire or toothed
flora_morphology.heads: Numerous tiny heads in narrow terminal paniculiform array; involucres 3–4 mm high, phyllaries four imbricated series per genus
flora_morphology.rays: 20–40 very inconspicuous whitish/cream/pinkish pistillate rays with limbs shorter than tube/pappus

source_conflicts_or_qa: Var. canadensis has spreading stem hairs and pilose leaf margins; var. glabrata glabrous stems; varieties not assumed for species-level photos.
Not to be confused with Conyza ramosissima (now Erigeron divaricatus).

flora_morphology.growth: Taprooted annual, 7–30 cm, spring peduncles <4 cm per key
flora_morphology.leaves: Alternate, narrow within Erigeron genus; detailed species blade measurements not given in 1999 paragraph
flora_morphology.rays: White to rosy/lavender; numerous narrow ray florets per genus
flora_morphology.fruit: Pappus two whorls, 10 scabrous bristles and about 10 short scales

source_conflicts_or_qa: Regional flora spells E. geiserii in the key and E. geiseri in the paragraph; preserve original printed variation.
Compare E. modestus with woody enlarged taproot and spring peduncles 4–12 cm.

flora_morphology.growth: Often grayish pubescent perennial 10–20(–30) cm, enlarged woody taproot
flora_morphology.leaves: Early deeply lobed crowded basal leaves; later narrow oblanceolate to linear-lanceolate foliage
flora_morphology.heads: Long bare flowering stems in earliest spring, followed by bushy much-branched late-season growth with shorter peduncles
flora_morphology.rays: Ligules about 4–8 mm (ray flowers pistillate fertile per genus)
flora_morphology.fruit: Pappus two whorls: longer bristles and shorter bristles/scales
flora_morphology.flowering: Apr–Oct, spring and fall shoot forms differ

source_conflicts_or_qa: Multiple seasonal growth forms are explicitly described in original flora; useful for crew training.
Compare E. geiseri annual sandy-ground plant with unenlarged taproot.

flora_morphology.leaves: Mid/upper leaves clasping, 4–20 mm wide, 2–4× as long as wide; lower leaves with broadly winged petioles
flora_morphology.heads: Involucres 4–6 mm high, disks 6–15 mm wide
flora_morphology.rays: Numerous white to pale-pink ligules about 5–10 mm
flora_morphology.fruit: Disk pappus a single whorl of roughly 20–30 bristles
flora_morphology.habitat: Low prairies, stream banks, calcareous clay

source_conflicts_or_qa: Existing learner record says annual/biennial/short-lived perennial (from FNA); regional flora states perennial. Retain source difference.
Clasping stem leaves most useful against E. strigosus, but requires close leaf node photograph.

flora_morphology.growth: Usually biennial, sometimes annual or occasionally perennial; regional key stems 30–70 cm
flora_morphology.leaves: Middle/upper leaves narrower than E. philadelphicus and not markedly clasping; linear-lanceolate, rounded teeth when present
flora_morphology.stems: Upper stem hairs mostly appressed or incurved per key
flora_morphology.rays: White (rarely bluish) ligules ≤6 mm, pistillate fertile
flora_morphology.fruit: Disk pappus two whorls (inner 10–15 bristles, outer minute scales); ray pappus minute
flora_morphology.taxa: Var. beyrichii: diffuse scant-leaved inflorescence with 2–3 mm involucres; var. strigosus: fuller leafy inflorescence and (2–)2.5–5 mm involucres

source_conflicts_or_qa: Regional flora reports varieties difficult to distinguish; do not assign varieties to unidentified photos.
Compare E. annuus spreading upper hairs and more conspicuously toothed leaves.

flora_morphology.leaves: Mostly opposite, narrowly ovate, petioles 10–30 mm
flora_morphology.fruit: Genus Eupatorium s.l.: blackish five-ribbed cypselae with persistent bristle pappus

source_conflicts_or_qa: 1999 genus circumscription broad; use species name unchanged but record original generic limits.
Compare Ageratina altissima (Eupatorium rugosum) with less evidently resin-dotted phyllaries.
